What is the difference between Swagger and OpenAPI?

OpenAPI is the specification, governed by the OpenAPI Initiative under the Linux Foundation. Swagger is the original name, now the brand for SmartBear's tools (UI, Editor, Codegen). Swagger 2.0 was renamed OpenAPI 2.0, and today you write OpenAPI 3.x documents and view them in Swagger UI.
How do you add Swagger to a Spring Boot 3 project?

Add springdoc-openapi-starter-webmvc-ui (2.x). No annotations are needed: the spec is at /v3/api-docs and the UI at /swagger-ui.html. Then enrich it with an OpenAPI bean (info, servers, security), @Tag/@Operation/@Schema, and permit those paths in Spring Security. Springfox doesn't work with Boot 3 because of the jakarta namespace and because it's no longer maintained.
How does springdoc generate the documentation?

At startup, or on the first request to /v3/api-docs, it inspects Spring's RequestMappingHandlerMapping to find every endpoint. It reads method signatures (@PathVariable, @RequestParam, @RequestBody, return types), uses Jackson to build schemas from DTOs, applies Bean Validation constraints, and merges in the Swagger annotations. The result is cached.
Code-first vs contract-first (API-first) — which is better?

Code-first (springdoc): fast, and the documentation always matches the code, but the API design happens implicitly. Contract-first: write api.yaml first, review it with consumers, and generate server interfaces and client SDKs with openapi-generator. Front-end and back-end teams can work in parallel against mocks (Prism), breaking changes show up in review, and the compiler enforces the contract. Contract-first is preferred for public or multi-team APIs.
How do you document JWT authentication in Swagger?

Define a security scheme: @SecurityScheme(name="bearerAuth", type=HTTP, scheme="bearer", bearerFormat="JWT"), or in the OpenAPI bean under components. Apply it globally with addSecurityItem or per operation with @SecurityRequirement(name="bearerAuth"). Swagger UI then shows an Authorize button. For OAuth2 you can configure the authorization code flow with PKCE so users can log in from the UI.
How do you hide endpoints or group APIs?

Hide them with @Hidden, or with the springdoc.paths-to-exclude or packages-to-scan settings. Group them with GroupedOpenApi beans (public, admin, internal), which appear as a dropdown in the UI with a separate spec URL each (/v3/api-docs/public).
Should Swagger UI be enabled in production?

Usually not for internal or private APIs: it reveals your attack surface. Options: springdoc.swagger-ui.enabled=false and api-docs.enabled=false in the prod profile, or keep it behind authentication or VPN-only access, or publish the spec to an internal developer portal instead. Public APIs often do publish their docs deliberately.
How do you show examples and error responses?

Use @Schema(example = "...") on fields, @ExampleObject inside @Content for full JSON examples, and @ApiResponse(responseCode="404", content=@Content(schema=@Schema(implementation=ProblemDetail.class))) for errors. You can also add global responses with an OperationCustomizer or OpenApiCustomizer bean.
How do you version APIs in OpenAPI docs?

Use one GroupedOpenApi per version (/api/v1/**, /api/v2/**), set info.version, and mark old operations with @Operation(deprecated = true), which Swagger UI shows struck through. Keep the spec files in Git and diff them in CI (openapi-diff) to catch breaking changes.
How can the Angular team use your OpenAPI spec?

Run openapi-generator with -g typescript-angular to get typed services and models (OrdersService.getOrder(id): Observable<OrderDto>), so nobody hand-writes HTTP calls or interfaces and type mismatches fail at compile time. Re-run it in CI whenever the spec changes.
Why does a generated client's method name keep changing?

The name comes from operationId, which springdoc derives from the Java method name, and de-duplicates with suffixes. Adding or moving a controller can shift those suffixes. Set an explicit @Operation(operationId = ...) on public operations.
How do you document a polymorphic request body?

Use @Schema(oneOf = {...}, discriminatorProperty = "type") with @DiscriminatorMapping, and matching Jackson @JsonTypeInfo and @JsonSubTypes so the runtime accepts what the document promises. Test both directions, since the annotations are independent.
How do you make sure the documented API matches the implementation?

Code-first generation stays close, but only reflects what is annotated: hand-written @ApiResponse values can be wrong. Add a contract test: validate real responses against the spec in integration tests, or run Schemathesis. For spec-first, generated interfaces let the compiler enforce signatures. Diff the spec in CI to catch accidental change.
What does OpenAPI 3.1 change? Why might you stay on 3.0?

3.1 is compatible with JSON Schema 2020-12, replaces nullable with type arrays, and adds webhooks. You might stay on 3.0 if generators, gateways or validators in your toolchain are not ready. springdoc can output either.
Swagger UI shows the wrong server URL or a CORS error in production. What do you check?

The spec's servers list usually holds the internal URL. Enable forwarded-header handling, or set servers explicitly. A CORS error comes from Try it out calling a different origin than the UI's, so align these, or allow that origin in the API's CORS configuration.
Swagger annotations vs REST Docs: how do you choose?

Annotations are quick, and give a live UI, but mix documentation with code and can drift. REST Docs is verified by tests, and can produce OpenAPI through a community extension, at the cost of writing those tests. Many teams prefer springdoc for internal APIs, and invest more in public ones.

The Angular client receives wrong times or rounded amounts. What in the spec might cause it?

Common causes: LocalDateTime is sent without an offset, and the browser interprets it in local time. BigDecimal becomes a TypeScript number (a double), which loses precision. Large long ids exceed Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER. Fix the API types, not the client: use Instant or OffsetDateTime, send money as a decimal string or as integer minor units, and expose large ids as strings. Then document the format with @Schema(type = "string", format = "...") where needed.
How do you document Kafka or other message-based interfaces?

Use AsyncAPI, the messaging counterpart of OpenAPI. It describes channels or topics, message payloads and headers, and who publishes or subscribes. Generate it with a tool like Springwolf, or write it contract-first. Combine it with a Schema Registry (Avro or Protobuf) that enforces backward compatibility, so that producers cannot break consumers. Publish both the OpenAPI and AsyncAPI documents in the same developer portal.
How do you document a field with dynamic keys, such as a map of attributes?

A Map<String, V> becomes type: object with additionalProperties set to the schema of V. Generators turn this into { [key: string]: V } in TypeScript, or into a Map in Java. If the keys are actually a fixed set, model them as a real class with named properties instead. That gives type safety and documentation for each field.
springdoc-openapi vs Springfox: why did projects migrate?

| springdoc-openapi | Springfox
Maintenance | Active | No release since 3.0.0 (2020)
Spring Boot 3 / Jakarta | Supported (springdoc 2.x and later) | Not supported
Spec version | OpenAPI 3.0 and 3.1 | Mainly Swagger 2.0, partial OpenAPI 3.0
Annotations | io.swagger.v3.oas.annotations (@Operation, @Schema) | Swagger 2 annotations (@ApiOperation, @ApiModel)
Setup | Add one starter, no config class needed | Docket bean
Interview tip: a Boot 2 to Boot 3 upgrade is when most teams switch. The work is mostly renaming annotations (@ApiOperation to @Operation, @ApiModelProperty to @Schema) and replacing the Docket with GroupedOpenApi beans.
required vs nullable vs readOnly in a schema: what does each promise?

| required | nullable | readOnly
Meaning | The key must be present | The value may be null | Sent in responses only, not accepted in requests
Where in the spec | List on the parent object | 3.0: nullable: true; 3.1: type includes "null" | On the property
Java side (springdoc) | @NotNull, @NotBlank or @Schema(requiredMode = REQUIRED) | @Schema(nullable = true) in 3.0 specs | @Schema(accessMode = READ_ONLY)
Generated TypeScript | name: string instead of name?: string | string | null | Often omitted from request models
Rule of thumb: required and nullable are independent: a field can be required and still allow null. Get them right, because the Angular team's generated types depend on them.
Swagger UI vs Redoc vs a Postman collection: which documentation for whom?

| Swagger UI | Redoc | Postman collection
Best for | Developers trying calls | Readable reference for partners | Testers and scripted flows
Try it out | Yes, built in | Not in the free version | Yes, with environments and variables
Source | The OpenAPI spec | The OpenAPI spec | Imported from the spec, then edited by hand
Drift risk | None, rendered live | None, rendered from the spec | High once edited separately
Rule of thumb: keep the OpenAPI spec as the single source and render it. Swagger UI for internal developers, Redoc for published docs, Postman only for test scenarios, regenerated from the spec rather than maintained by hand.
openapi-generator vs swagger-codegen vs a hand-written Angular service?

| openapi-generator | swagger-codegen | Hand-written
Origin | Community fork of swagger-codegen (2018) | Original, maintained by SmartBear | Your team
Generators | Largest set, including typescript-angular and spring | Smaller set | n/a
Contract changes | Regenerate, compiler shows breakages | Regenerate | Found at runtime, or by tests
Control over code | Templates and options | Templates | Full
Rule of thumb: generate the models and services with openapi-generator in the build, pin the generator version, and wrap generated services in a thin hand-written layer if you need custom behaviour. Stable operationIds keep method names from changing.
